response.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        b.player_id,
        p.bats AS batting_hand,
        AVG(b."double") AS average_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS b
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = b.player_id
    GROUP BY b.player_id, p.bats
),
indexed AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        batting_hand,
        average_doubles,
        average_doubles / AVG(average_doubles) OVER () AS relative_index
    FROM player_averages
),
with_gaps AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        batting_hand,
        average_doubles,
        relative_index,
        relative_index - AVG(relative_index) OVER (PARTITION BY batting_hand) AS gap
    FROM indexed
)
SELECT player_id, batting_hand, average_doubles, relative_index, gap
FROM with_gaps
ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A postseason batting record is one row in batting_postseason; each player's average uses all such rows, and SQL AVG ignores null doubles. Players without any non-null doubles are therefore excluded from the averages and ranking.
